articles.title: OpenAI's isolated red-team AI agents built a hidden CPU cache channel to talk with no network or shared files — exploited CPU cache timing to bypass microVM sandboxes
articles.summary:
OpenAI's isolated red-team AI agents built a hidden CPU cache channel to talk with no network or shared files — exploited CPU cache timing to bypass microVM sandboxes
A hijacked AI agent could use the same technique to leak data without touching the network.
OpenAI’s AI agents built hidden channels to talk across walls put up between them in red-team tests, communicating by manipulating the CPU cache with no network link or shared file, according to a company blog post. The containment was intended to stop that kind of secret-swapping, but the agents found multiple ways around it when asked. Security researchers already showed that a covert cache channel can move data between cloud virtual machines (VMs); a hijacked agent on a shared cloud server could, in theory, exchange data on the same physical machine, and do so undetected by network monitoring.
The agents in question were set up in separate microVMs, on shared hosts, with OpenAI’s sandboxing software, and were asked to swap synthetic secrets without a network connection or shared writable files. One agent evicted select data from the CPU’s cache while another timed the reloading, enabling the two to communicate with fast and slow reads using a protocol they agreed on first. The same cache-timing technique was used to extract data in the Spectre and Meltdown attacks; but unlike in those cases, the covert channel here needs two willing parties.

articles.title: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions the Ukrainian military’s of use Starshield — the military-grade version of the company’s Starlink internet system.
The Wall Street Journal reports that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara told reporters that Starshield appears to be working normally again, although the military is still conducting tests and has not received an explanation for the restrictions.
This follows a 10-day period where Ukrainian drones would lose internet connectivity when flying at speeds of around 100 miles per hour, resulting in the military losing control of some drones, while others became more vulnerable because they were flying more slowly.
President Donald Trump reportedly called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to restore Starshield service. Both Trump and Musk have criticized Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, with Musk recently posting, “Zelensky has gone too far.”
The WSJ previously reported that Musk ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s Starlink access, though some sources claimed he’d discussed it with the Trump administration first. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine had “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people.”
“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk said. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”

New CD players keep launching, but a drive shortage could make them unfixable — almost nobody makes the drives anymore
CD player manufacturers are relying on a shrinking base of optical drive manufacturers.
Even as optical media sees a resurgence and new CD players hit the market, some optical drive and component manufacturers have ended production. As a result, PS Audio and Naim have halted production of their high-end CD players, raising questions about the maintenance and repairability of these new devices. Headphonesty says that of the eight new models, four are from Musical Fidelity, two from Marantz, and one each from Arcam and NAD.
Musical Fidelity reportedly sources its key components from SUOS-HiFi, with three of its new models using SUOS disc mechanisms. In contrast, the fourth uses a SUOS-sourced servo but a tray-loading mechanism from an unnamed manufacturer. On the other hand, Marantz reportedly develops its drives in-house, though it’s unclear whether it also outsources production to a third party. As for the two remaining manufacturers, they did not reveal who made their optical drives.
PS Audio had to end production of the PMG Super Audio CD Transport because D&M, Marantz’s parent company, has ceased external orders for its optical drives. Although the company bought D&M’s entire remaining stock, it wasn’t enough to keep production going. Sony Patent Turns Game Audio Into Visual Cues for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing Players
A newly published Sony Interactive Entertainment patent application, titled "Audio Processing System and Method," describes a way to turn in-game sounds into visual cues for players who are deaf or hard of hearing. The system classifies the intended effect of a sound before it plays, such as building fear or tension, warning of danger, or describing the environment, and then displays a matching visual element. That could be an icon, a shape, or even an onomatopoeic word like "Roar!" for a nearby monster. Properties such as color, brightness, or transparency are tied to the sound's volume and character. 
The patent also describes directional lighting to show where a sound is coming from, either as LEDs around the display or as LEDs encircling the touchpad on a DualSense controller. The application, published on October 22, is a continuation of a US application filed in May 2023, which in turn claims priority from a UK filing dating back to June 2022. One interesting detail is support for older games, since the patent suggests the operating system or a helper app could tag a legacy game's sound files and generate the cues without changes to the game's code.Sony has filed several accessibility-focused patents lately, including one for AI that fills in controller inputs for players with physical limitations. YouTube Sets Early 2027 Target for AV2 Streams on the Web
The Alliance for Open Media (AOMedia) shared an update on AV2 this week, and the clearest date in it comes from YouTube. Des Keane, Engineering Director at YouTube, confirmed the platform will begin streaming in AV2, which is the royalty-free successor to AV1 that AOMedia says offers roughly 30% better compression. In practice, that means either sharper video at the same bitrate or the same quality using less bandwidth, and the codec also adds support for multi-stream and multi-view video, higher frame rates, and improved HDR. Keane put it plainly: "YouTube AV2 streams will be available for Web as soon as early 2027."
Chrome is the other half. Jim Bankoski, VP of Engineering for Google Chrome, said AV2 playback has been demonstrated in the browser, though Google hasn't said which Chrome version will get it or whether it will be on by default. That demo dates back to CES 2026, where Google streamed AV2 videos from YouTube to a gaming laptop at 1080p and 24 FPS using a custom Chrome build with the reference decoder. Netflix and Prime Video are also exploring the format, but neither has shared a timeline. Meta wants to repeat its AV1 rollout with AV2, and Intel is working on SVT-AV2.In terms of hardware, it looks like no consumer GPU or TV supports AV2 hardware decoding yet, so early playback will probably lean on the CPU. articles.title: Pensilvania obligará a etiquetar los avisos publicitarios hechos o editados con inteligencia artificial
articles.summary:
El gobernador de Pensilvania, Josh Shapiro, firmó la Ley de Publicidad Engañosa con Inteligencia Artificial, que obliga a las empresas a avisar cuando un aviso publicitario fue creado o modificado de forma significativa con esta tecnología. La norma entrará en vigencia el 21 de diciembre de 2026.
La ley abarca a imágenes, videos, audios y textos generados o editados con inteligencia artificial que se muestren a consumidores del estado, sin importar dónde se haya producido el aviso. Pensilvania se convierte así en uno de los primeros estados de Estados Unidos en exigir este tipo de advertencia.
“Si ves un aviso en Facebook o en internet y fue generado con inteligencia artificial, tienen que poner una advertencia abajo que diga que fue generado con IA”, explicó el senador estatal Nick Pisciottano, autor del proyecto, a CBS News.
Qué dice la nueva ley
El texto de la ley exige que la advertencia se muestre la primera vez que el contenido sintético aparece ante el consumidor, en el mismo formato del aviso, y que sea permanente o muy difícil de eliminar cuando sea técnicamente posible.
La obligación alcanza tanto a comerciales televisivos de grandes empresas como a folletos de promociones de restaurantes locales, siempre que el contenido sintético pueda generar una percepción falsa sobre el origen o la autenticidad de lo que se vende.
La norma deja algunas excepciones: no aplica a contenido “evidentemente ficticio”, a parodias, sátiras, críticas o comentarios, ni a publicidad limit…

La pequeña Suecia en Mallorca da buena cuenta de este modus vivendi. Ese perfil acaba de perder su primer puesto. Durante los seis primeros meses de 2026, según datos del Notariado, la nacionalidad que más vivienda española compra es la marroquí: 4.960 operaciones frente a las 4.541 de los británicos.
Un sorpasso por 419 casas. En 2025 los británicos todavía iban ganando (10.925 viviendas contra 10.829). En el segundo semestre de ese año, por 24 operaciones. Detrás de Marruecos van Reino Unido, Italia (4.109), Rumanía (3.974) y Alemania (3.907). Las cinco suman el 34,6% de las compras de extranjeros, y los marroquíes aportan el 8%.
Uno veranea, el otro vive. Aquí empieza lo interesante: de las 4.960 compras marroquíes, 4.897 (el 98,7%) las hacen residentes. De las 4.541 británicas, 2.388 (el 52,6%) son de gente que vive fuera. Marruecos es además la mayor comunidad extranjera con permiso en vigor: 910.001 personas. Y hay regiones, como algunos pueblos de Cáceres, donde superan a la población española. El Tribunal Supremo ha dictaminado que el uso de la tarjeta bancaria de otra persona nunca es un delito leve, ni siquiera cuando la cantidad es mínima. Y es que tal y como comparte el medio El Economista, a un hombre que gastó 31,50 euros con una tarjeta robada en un bar de Girona se le ha restituido su condena de seis meses de prisión.
Por qué es importante. Hasta ahora, muchos tribunales trataban este tipo de fraudes como un “delito leve”, pues no superaba la cantidad de 400 euros y, según la ley española, se castiga únicamente con una multa. Sin embargo, la Sala de lo Penal del Tribunal Supremo ha cerrado esa puerta, pues en la sentencia 565/2026, de 25 de septiembre, sostuvo que el uso fraudulento de tarjetas es un delito independiente con sus propias penas, y que el umbral de los 400 euros simplemente no se le aplica.

Unos 15 minutos después, un hombre pagó tres consumiciones de 10,50 euros cada una con su tarjeta en el bar de al lado, acercándola al datáfono, según se puede leer en la sentencia. Tras ello, la dueña de la tarjeta la bloqueó, habiéndose rechazado un nuevo intento de pago de 120 euros.
La Policía Municipal lo detuvo en el acto y fue condenado por los pagos con la tarjeta, pero fue absuelto del robo del bolso, al no haberse acreditado cómo llegó la tarjeta a su poder.

Investigadores de la Universidad Estatal de Ohio y del Laboratorio de Zhejiang desarrollaron un sistema experimental que detecta olores mediante inteligencia artificial y los reproduce cerca de la nariz de otra persona a través de internet.
El trabajo, descrito en la revista ‘Science Advances’, combina detección química, aprendizaje automático y dispositivos portátiles con forma de pulseras o collares.
En pruebas de laboratorio con 14 voluntarios sanos, los participantes identificaron olores individuales con un 73% de precisión y combinaciones de dos aromas con un 71%. Estos resultados marcan un paso hacia la incorporación del olfato a las experiencias digitales, aunque el sistema depende todavía de aromas pregrabados y no puede reconstruir olores arbitrarios desde cero.
El desafío de digitalizar un olor
Reproducir un olor plantea un problema distinto al de transmitir imágenes o sonido. Las cámaras y los micrófonos capturan ondas de luz y sonido, mientras que los olores se originan en compuestos químicos que deben detectarse y liberarse físicamente para que una persona pueda percibirlos.
Los métodos previos para transmitir aromas incluían equipos de escritorio voluminosos, tarjetas con fragancias y gafas de realidad virtual, varios de los cuales requerían que el receptor liberara el olor de forma manual. El nuevo sistema busca automatizar ese proceso de principio a fin.

I bring up Nolan because XPAN mode turned what would have been good-but-not-great vacation snaps into photos that look like scenes from The Odyssey.

La romancière sud-africaine annonce 371 titres et défend ouvertement sa méthode, alors que l’éditeur québécois de Thélyson Orélien vient de rompre avec lui en l’accusant d’avoir écrit son roman avec l’IA, ce qu’il dément.
Deux salles, deux ambiances. Les Éditions du Boréal ne réimprimeront pas C’était ça ou mourir et ne publieront plus Thélyson Orélien. Après avoir fait expertiser ses versions de travail, la maison québécoise dit avoir trouvé « des traces de balises d’IA » dans les métadonnées de plusieurs fichiers, sans savoir quel rôle l’IA a joué dans le roman. « Le livre a été écrit par moi », a répondu à Libération l’écrivain, qui reconnaît seulement avoir utilisé l’IA pour des recherches historiques.
Coral Hart n’a pas attendu qu’un éditeur fouille ses fichiers pour raconter comment elle produit ses romans. « J’ai choisi d’être celle qui se montre et dit : il faut avoir ces discussions », explique-t-elle à l’AFP. Ses chiffres de vente ne sont vérifiés par personne, et les acheteurs de ses livres sur Amazon n’ont aucun moyen de savoir qu’une IA a écrit le premier jet de leur roman.

articles.title: Un article scientifique sur Z-Library cite un article de presse qui n’existe pas
articles.summary:
Deux bibliothécaires d’universités nigérianes citent, dans une étude sur Z-Library publiée par une revue à comité de lecture, un article de TorrentFreak que le site d’information sur le piratage n’a jamais écrit. Au total, au moins dix des 44 références de l’étude sont introuvables, et ses auteurs reconnaissent avoir travaillé avec deux outils d’IA.
Malgré les blocages ordonnés par la justice, des millions de livres et d’articles piratés sont toujours téléchargeables gratuitement sur Z-Library, par des adresses personnelles ou le réseau Tor. Des étudiants et des chercheurs qui ne peuvent pas payer leurs manuels les récupèrent sur le site, et les éditeurs scientifiques multiplient les procédures contre lui. Les deux bibliothécaires examinent ce conflit sans prendre parti dans leur étude, parue début octobre dans la New Review of Academic Librarianship, chez l’éditeur Taylor & Francis. L’auteur principal a envoyé un exemplaire du texte à Ernesto Van der Sar, fondateur de TorrentFreak. D’après l’étude, Elsevier et Springer Nature ont attaqué Z-Library en justice, preuve à l’appui d’un article de TorrentFreak paru en 2021. Le titre est inventé, et la référence se contente d’un lien vers la page d’accueil du site. Les relecteurs de la revue n'y ont vu que du feu et n’ont repéré ni cette fausse source ni les autres.

The primary objective behind deploying the malware is to undermine Microsoft Windows startup defenses, along with third-party security solutions, while maintaining long-term, covert access to compromised devices.
Notably, BlackX is assessed to be an updated version of BlackLotus, a notorious bootkit that was first observed being advertised on cybercrime forums in late 2022, before its existence was officially confirmed by ESET in March 2023.
BlackLotus is designed to exploit a now-patched Secure Boot bypass vulnerability tracked as CVE-2022-21894 (CVSS score: 4.4), also known as Baton Drop, to load malicious code before the operating system starts. However, successful exploitation hinges on an attacker having administrator privileges or physical access to a target host.

articles.title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
articles.summary:
Between November 2025 and March 2026, the Dutch security firm Eye Security pushed more than 2 million updates to computers it did not own to switch off a background updater that it said could have allowed an outsider to take over the machine.
The updater belongs to Time4Popcorn, an abandoned copy of Popcorn Time, a free app that streamed pirated films and TV over BitTorrent.
Popcorn Time was popular about a decade ago, and the original shut down in 2014, but several copies kept running under the same name. A separate, legal project that took the Popcorn Time name in early 2025 is unrelated to it.
Eye Security, which monitors client networks for threats, found the updater during a routine threat hunt: a program called Updater.exe on one client's laptop kept trying to reach a web address that was no longer registered.
The firm registered the address itself to see what would connect, and about 50 requests a second poured in. It later laid out the operation, which it named Operation IXIM, in a write-up and a talk at Hack.lu on October 22.
Over six months, those requests carried more than 3.8 million different hardware IDs. The IDs proved an unreliable way to count machines, because some Windows PCs shared one and some Macs changed theirs, so Eye revised its estimate to 2.5 to 3 million Windows computers and 250,000 to 350,000 Macs.
The updater ran in the background on Windows and Mac from the moment the computer started. It checked for new versions over an unencrypted connection …

articles.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
articles.summary:
A memory-corruption flaw in Google's Brotli decoder sits in many programs that unpack Brotli-compressed data, among them Bun, the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages, and Envoy proxies set up to decompress Brotli.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, the flaw allows crafted compressed data to overwrite past the end of a buffer and corrupt a program's memory, potentially causing a crash, a memory leak, or the execution of attacker-controlled code.
Imperva researchers have shown that code can run on one unpatched Node.js build. The same has not been demonstrated on the other software, and no real-world attacks have been reported.
The flaw was first disclosed on October 21, when Node.js and Google shipped fixes, and more have followed product by product since. Because the bug is in Google's decoder and each program ships its own copy of it, every one has to update that copy on its own.
Brotli is a compression format from Google, used across the web to shrink pages and other traffic. The bug is in the C code that unpacks a Brotli stream, so it travels into anything that reuses that code, from language runtimes to proxies to Python packages.
